key_insight: A deep-learning-driven framework can discover and de novo generate functional internal ribosome entry sites (IRES), enabling programmable control of RNA translation and validated at scale with high-throughput functional assays.
problem_solved: Current methods lack scalable, predictive ways to identify and design IRES elements for precise translation control, limiting engineering of RNA therapeutics and synthetic gene circuits. This work provides an end-to-end platform to map sequence→function and rationally create functional IRES sequences.
method: Generate large-scale sequence-to-function data for IRES activity using high-throughput functional assays of extensive libraries.
Train deep learning models to predict IRES activity and perform de novo sequence generation/optimization for desired translation profiles.
Experimentally validate model-designed IRES variants with high-throughput assays to demonstrate programmable translation control.
impact: Demonstrates a template for combining ML with high-throughput experimentation to design functional biological sequences, accelerating RNA therapeutic design and sequence-level control in synthetic biology. It highlights opportunities for ML practitioners to apply generative and predictive models to molecular engineering problems.

paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
